kurzfassung: Former CIA targeting officer Sarah Adams analyzes the case of an ISIS member who carried out a fatal attack at Old Dominion University after being released from prison. She discusses the lack of monitoring for freed terrorists and institutional blind spots regarding criminal history. The conversation also highlights broader national security concerns involving online recruitment and released extremists.
stichpunkte: Sarah Adams explains her background as a CIA targeter and her independent investigation into terror attacks
Mohamed Baylor Jalloh was convicted in 2016 for an ISIS attack plot and sentenced to 11 years
Jalloh's sentence was shortened, and he was released on supervised release in December 2024
Old Dominion University had no knowledge of his criminal history due to state laws and lack of notification
Virginia law prohibited asking about criminal history during admissions, and the parole officer had no legal duty to inform the school
Adams notes that 72 individuals convicted of joining ISIS have been released in the United States
The Bureau of Prisons changed policy to exclude terrorism offenders from early release programs tied to drug rehabilitation
The United States currently lacks a public registry for convicted terrorists similar to sex offender registries

clips.hook: An 11-year prison sentence shortened and a released ISIS member walking free
clips.text: The guest details the 2016 conviction of an extremist involved in an active military targeting plot and explains how his prison term was reduced before his late 2024 release.

clips.hook: Dozens of imprisoned ISIS supporters have already returned to American streets
clips.text: The former intelligence officer reveals that a significant number of individuals convicted of joining ISIS have finished their terms and reentered society largely unmonitored.

clips.hook: No laws require parole officers to warn schools about enrolled ISIS members
clips.text: The discussion highlights the absence of legal mandates requiring authorities to disclose a student's terrorist background to educational institutions.

clips.hook: How modern online recruitment makes terrorism more accessible than ever
clips.text: The expert points out that shifts in extremist tactics allow individuals to engage in terrorist activities digitally without needing to travel overseas.

clips.hook: Why communities lack a public registry to track convicted terrorists
clips.text: The conversation draws attention to the absence of a tracking system for freed extremists comparable to databases used for sex offenders.

beschreibung:
Former CIA targeting officer Sarah Adams joins Morning Wire to break down the Old Dominion University terror attack that left an Army ROTC instructor dead and two cadets injured. Adams details how suspect Mohamed Bailor Jalloh returned to campus despite his criminal history, what happened during the attack, and why researchers were warning of a growing ISIS-era terrorism threat in the U.S. Get the facts first with Morning Wire.
